findings.title: Two contradictory `step()` implementations; the second skips `post_tick()` when there are no entities
findings.description: The document gives two versions of `SimulationManager.step()`. The "SimulationManager as Simulation Orchestrator" snippet (lines 176-190) guards only `engine.tick()` with `if self._entity_manager.count > 0:` and calls `post_tick()` unconditionally — correct. The "Implementation Details" snippet (lines 270-288) instead uses `if self._entity_manager.count == 0: return` placed *after* `pre_tick()` and *before* `engine.tick()`. With that version, a zero-entity tick returns before reaching `post_tick()`, so `post_tick()` is never called. This directly contradicts the note on line 291 ("post_tick() is called even when there are no entities. The early return is moved to wrap only engine.tick()"), the functional requirement on line 347, and the task file's test "step() calls post_tick() even when entity count is zero." Because time-varying layers (trail decay) must advance with no agents present, an implementer who follows the second snippet produces silently wrong behavior. Pick one snippet and make the zero-entity path call `pre_tick()` and `post_tick()` around a skipped `engine.tick()`.

findings.title: "Layers register themselves / plug in without server changes" conflicts with the provider architecture's construction-time composition
findings.description: The overview (line 19) and "Provides to Other Slices" (line 329) promise that layers "plug in without server changes" and "register themselves," but the design hard-codes `Environment(bounds=world_bounds, layers={})` in `server.py` (lines 97, 303). `500-arch.environment-layer.md` explicitly states "Extension through data, not plugins — ... The environment layer does not provide a dynamic layer registry or abstract plugin interface. Layers are statically composed in the environment container," and `500-slice.grid-infrastructure-and-world-coordinates.md` constructs `Environment(bounds, layers)` with layers "composed at construction." Under that contract, each layer slice that becomes ready (501-507) will require editing this construction site in `server.py`. The design neither explains the composition mechanism nor reconciles it with the static-composition principle, leaving a hidden dependency for the consuming/serving slices. Either state that layer slices must update the construction site (and drop the "no server changes" claim) or specify the intended composition hook.

findings.title: The plan's "pass environment context to `engine.tick()`" is not done literally; resolved via constructor injection
findings.description: The parent plan (300-slices, entry 304) assigns "Pass environment context to `SimulationManager` and `engine.tick()`." This slice passes the `Environment` to `SimulationManager` and exposes it via a property (lines 264-266, 300), but `engine.tick(state, profiles, spatial, dt, forces)` (line 104) receives no environment argument — and the slice-100 `tick()` signature has no such parameter. The design resolves this by injecting the environment into forces via constructor (lines 202-215), which is consistent with the architecture's "forces query the environment" model and defers environment-aware forces as excluded scope. This is a defensible resolution of the plan's intent, but it is a deliberate divergence worth recording: no force in this slice actually queries the environment, so the integration point is established but not exercised until a future behavior slice.

findings.title: "bounds shared with entity manager" is inaccurate
findings.description: State Management describes `bounds: WorldBounds` as "immutable world boundaries, shared with entity manager." In the design, the entity manager was created earlier from `WorldBoundsConfig` (slice 303, and unchanged here per the Component Structure), while this slice builds a separate `WorldBounds` via `build_world_bounds()` and passes only that one to `Environment`. Nothing shares a `WorldBounds` instance between the two components. Minor, but given the architecture's "authoritative state ownership" goal, the doc should not imply a single shared bounds object when two derived-from-config instances exist.

structured_findings.summary: Two contradictory `step()` implementations; the second skips `post_tick()` when there are no entities
"Layers register themselves / plug in without server changes" conflicts with the provider architecture's construction-time composition
The plan's "pass environment context to `engine.tick()`" is not done literally; resolved via constructor injection
"bounds shared with entity manager" is inaccurate
